en.title: When the Roll Is Called Up Yonder
en.author: James M. Black
stanzas:
[G]When the trumpet of the Lord shall sound, and [C]time shall be no [G]more,
And the morning breaks, eternal, bright and [D]fair;
[G]When the saved of earth shall gather over [C]on the other [G]shore,
And the roll is called up [D7]yonder, I'll be [G]there.

On that bright and cloudless morning when the dead in Christ shall rise,
And the glory of His resurrection share;
When His chosen ones shall gather to their home beyond the skies,
And the roll is called up yonder, I'll be there.

Let us labor for the Master from the dawn till setting sun,
Let us talk of all His wondrous love and care;
Then when all of life is over, and our work on earth is done,
And the roll is called up yonder, I'll be there.
en.chorus:
When the [G]roll is called up yonder,
When the [D7]roll is called up yonder,
When the [G]roll is called up [C]yonder,
When the [G]roll is called up [D7]yonder, I'll be [G]there.

notes: Text from Timeless Truths (Evening Light Songs #507). Hymnary's representative text (Our Great Redeemer's Praise #624) has the same three stanzas and refrain, differing only in line-initial capitals and two line-end marks. TT offers 'sabbath morning' as an alternate for 'cloudless morning' in stanza 2; 'cloudless' is the 1893 reading and ships. Tune ROLL CALL, meter 15.11.15.11 with refrain. Key: hymnary's instances run 40 A-flat to 15 G (9 G plus 6 'G or modal') and 1 A; TT prints A-flat. Moved to G for guitar per the key rule (G is a semitone away and first in the preference order). Chords derived from the Timeless Truths MusicXML score by reading the four-part chord on every beat, transposed A-flat to G. Stanza: I, with V/A and I/B walking the bass under 'sound' dropped, IV6 on 'time shall be no', I, a cluster of passing chords on 'bright and' dropped, V on 'fair', the same again, then I6/4-V7-I. Refrain: the score opens each 'roll' on a one-beat iii or ii (Bm, Am) before settling; the harmonic rhythm underneath is I | V7 | I IV | I V7 I, which is what the chart carries.
